jobs.title: Data Scientist (f/m/div.)
jobs.jd: Your contribution to something big: You will contribute to an industrial research project focused on developing machine learning and AI solutions to predict and optimize energy consumption in residential heating systems. You will work across the full AI lifecycle, from data collection and feature engineering to model development, validation, and deployment. You will also explore Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), and AI Agents to develop intelligent applications and automate engineering workflows, collaborating closely with R&D, thermal simulation, controls, and software teams. Your main responsibilities will be: Machine Learning Development: Design, develop, and validate machine learning models to predict residential heating system energy consumption, including hourly consumption, peak loads, and longer-term energy demand. Data Engineering & Feature Development: Work with sensor data, weather information, building characteristics, occupancy data, and other relevant sources to prepare datasets and develop meaningful features. Data Quality & Analysis: Clean and analyse complex sensor and IoT datasets, identifying missing or inconsistent data and addressing seasonal effects and changes in operating conditions. Modeling & Forecasting: Develop and compare different approaches, including regression, time-series forecasting, gradient boosting, neural networks, physics-informed models, and hybrid solutions. Generative AI & AI Agents: Explore and develop AI applications using LLMs, prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and AI agents to support data analysis, knowledge extraction, intelligent automation, and engineering workflows. Model Validation & Optimization: Evaluate and continuously improve ML and AI solutions through experimentation, error analysis, performance evaluation, and robustness testing. ML/AI Deployment & Monitoring: Support the integration of ML and AI solutions into production environments, contributing to monitoring, model performance evaluation, and continuous improvement. Cross-functional Collaboration: Work closely with thermal modelling, HVAC, controls, and software engineers to translate complex engineering challenges into data science and AI solutions. Technical Guidance & Documentation: Support junior team members and document modelling approaches, AI architectures, results, assumptions, and technical trade-offs. What distinguishes you: Experience: Around 3 years of experience in Data Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field. Machine Learning: Good knowledge of machine learning, statistical methods, and predictive modelling, including regression, classification, and time-series forecasting. Generative AI & LLMs: Knowledge or practical experience with LLMs, Generative AI applications, prompt engineering, and RAG. AI Agents : Understanding AI agent architectures and the integration of LLMs with external tools, APIs, and data sources is a plus. Programming: Strong Python skills and experience with tools such as scikit-learn, XGBoost, PyTorch, TensorFlow, or AI development frameworks. Data Analysis: Experience working with complex datasets, including data cleaning, feature engineering, and analysis. Experience with sensor or IoT data is a plus. ML/AI Deployment: Understanding of model deployment, monitoring, and MLOps/LLMOps concepts. Technical Knowledge: Experience with time-series forecasting, physics-informed ML, HVAC/thermal systems, or IoT applications is considered an advantage. Problem Solving & Collaboration: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, good communication skills, and ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary engineering and software teams. Working Style: Proactive, structured, and comfortable taking ownership of assigned activities and supporting junior team members. Work #LikeABosch includes: ⚖️ Flexible work conditions 🔀 Hybrid work system 🌐 Exchange with colleagues around the world 🧑‍⚕️ Health insurance and medical office on site (general surgeon, psychology, physiotherapy, general clinic) 📚 Training opportunities (p.e., technical training, foreign languages training) & certifications 📈 Opportunities for career progression and continuous professional development 💲 Access to great discounts in partnerships and Bosch products 🏋️ Sports and health related activities 💰 Flexible benefits platform 🅿️ Free parking lot 🍽️ Canteen Success stories don´t just happen. They are made... Make it happen! We are looking forward to your application!

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer II - Agentic Intelligence
jobs.jd: What We’re Building Honeycomb is a service for the near and present future, defining observability and raising expectations of what developer tools can do! We’re working with well known companies like HelloFresh, Slack, LaunchDarkly, and Vanguard and more across a range of industries. This is an exciting time in our trajectory, we’ve closed Series D funding, scaled past the 200-person mark, and were named to Forbes’ America’s Best Startups of 2022 and 2023! If you want to see what we’ve been up to, please check out these blog posts and Honeycomb .io press releases. Who We Are We come for the impact, and stay for the culture! We’re a talented, opinionated, passionate, fiercely inclusive, and responsible group of bees. We have conviction and we strive to live our values every day. We want our people to do what they truly love amongst a team of highly talented (but humble) peers. How We Work We are a fully distributed company, which means we believe it is not where you sit, but how you deliver that matters most. We invest in our people and care about how you orient to our culture and processes. At the same time we imbue a lot of trust, autonomy, and accountability from Day 1. Little more about the team: AI agents at Honeycomb investigate, reason, and act on real observability data. They live in Canvas: the agentic workspace where engineers go to understand their systems. The Agentic Intelligence team has shipped Canvas, the Honeycomb MCP server, and the Canvas Agent and Canvas Skills surfaces. What we're looking for today is someone who brings deep agent expertise and uses it to expand what the team can build: new agents, new surface area in Canvas, memory, spatial awareness, improved performance on our Bedrock loop. Honeycomb 's data store is fast and accepts high cardinality data; that's what makes agents built on top of it different from anything built on a conventional observability backend. This role is about taking advantage of that building agents that can do things no other observability product can do because the underlying data makes it possible. Some of this work will start as a prototype. The expectation is that the code makes it through the full arc, from the rough first version through to something that holds up in production. What you'll do Design and deliver production-grade agents. Build agents that investigate, reason, and act on live observability data inside Canvas. These agents must be trustworthy to engineers in high pressure situations, including mid-incident. Take one from rough first version to something that holds up under production traffic. Own the agent work; support the whole product. Scope, build, ship, and maintain the agents including the evals that tell you whether they got better or are just different. This role is agent-focused and also includes some fullstack development. Build agents only Honeycomb can build. Use a data store that returns high-cardinality queries in seconds to reason over signal a conventional backend can't serve at this fidelity correlating across services, drilling into a single trace, comparing before and after a deploy. Extend the surface, and decide what's next. Ship new capability into Canvas, the MCP server, and Canvas Skills memory, spatial awareness, a faster Bedrock loop and make the case for what comes after with working code. Distinguish hype from signal in a field with plenty of both. Define what "good" means for agents here. Set the bar: measurable against real evals, maintainable, and honest about their limits. Example projects Multiple agents collaborating on one shared Canvas investigation each claiming a hypothesis, publishing findings, and narrowing the search space for the others so it resolves faster (blog). Auto-investigation the moment an SLO burn alert fires the agent forms hypotheses and prepares visualizations before a human looks, cutting mean-time-to-insight for on-call (o11ycon 2026). Skills that encode a team's domain expertise e.g. Kubernetes thresholds so agents and human colleagues can lean on them (o11ycon 2026). What you'll bring: AI and agent engineering experience. You've shipped LLM-based systems people relied on in production not demos, not fine-tuned models in a research context. You know where agent systems break and how to design around it. End-to-end ownership. On a small team there's no handoff queue. You can take something from rough prototype to production-grade without needing someone behind you to do the durable engineering. Current judgment, not just past experience. You have informed opinions about what's shifted in agent design in the last six to twelve months that would change how you'd build today. Agent architecture depth. You understand how a fast, high-cardinality data store changes what an agent can reason about, and how to design for that. Product judgment. You can look at what the agent layer does today and see what it should do next and make that case with a prototype, not a deck. Even better Observability or developer-tools background. Engineers are your users; you'll ramp faster with fluency in that world, and the work is better. Familiarity with eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG, and prompt engineering. Base Salary based on level of experience $250,000—$280,000 CAD What you'll get when you join the Hive: A stake in our success - generous equity with employee-friendly stock program It’s not about how strong of a negotiator you are - our pay is based on transparent levels relative to experience Time to recharge with unlimited PTO A distributed-first mindset and culture (really!) Home office, co-working, and internet stipend Full benefits coverage for employees, with additional coverage available for dependents Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave, regardless of path to parenthood Annual development allowance And much more... Implement observability instrumentation within the application and agent code, continuously monitoring system behavior to act on anomalies and degradation. - Review and critique AI-generated outputs, ensuring adherence to technical, quality and business requirements before delivery. - Delegate specialized tasks to the agents they build, working with a generalist view across the whole development line, while sustaining technical depth and authority in their specialty stack to critically assess and validate outputs. - Deliver the solution in a production-ready state, aligned with the AI Deployment Engineer on deployment and operation requirements. - Apply ethics, privacy, data security and compliance practices, to keep the solutions within the client's and CI&T's rules. - Establish and reuse across the team (not only for themselves) the agents, skills and harness. - Structure orchestration and runtime frameworks, ensuring reliable inputs and behavior at scale. - Guide prompt engineering, evals and red teaming decisions at scale. - jobs.jd: About Watershed Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team. We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us! The role Forward Deployed Energy Engineers are a new role at Watershed, combining energy and advisory expertise with product-building skills and commercial instinct. You’ll operate at the cutting edge with Watershed customers to build and deploy the next generation of enterprise energy management. Energy is one of the largest costs on a big company’s P&L and one of its largest sources of emissions. Yet most enterprises have no one who owns how energy is purchased, consumed and reduced across all their sites. Watershed is building the product that changes that, and it’s the company’s biggest bet for its next chapter. We already help many of the world’s largest companies measure and cut their emissions, and our clean energy business has executed more than $100M in purchases. Now we’re building energy management from zero to one, with engagements underway with a small group of customers today and scaling in 2027. You’ll work with enterprises that spend tens of millions a year on electricity, embedded in their energy programmes. Starting from the energy data already in Watershed, you’ll find where they’re overspending, deliver the savings, prototype with AI what should become product, and help customers implement solutions, including buying clean power. The goal is an energy programme that wins backing from their CFO and facilities teams. This is a high-ownership role on a small, high-output team, with a direct line to commercial outcomes and real say in what we build. It reports directly to Watershed’s head of energy and decarbonization. What you'll do Deliver energy engagements with measurable results: Run deep engagements with a handful of customers at a time: change tariffs, upgrade equipment, find and cut waste, and show the savings. Win customers who vouch for us: Earn the trust of facilities and finance leads so they would tell a peer to work with Watershed. Turn what works into product: Spot the problems that repeat across customers, prototype with AI, and work with our engineers to build an AI-led product for many. Close clean energy deals: Help customers sign deals with existing clean power products (eg EACs, fixed-price VPPAs), yourself or alongside our account teams. Make the team smarter on energy: Be the person colleagues go to on tariffs, loads and what actually cuts a bill. You might be a fit if you Know how commercial and industrial sites use and buy energy (tariffs, loads, HVAC and controls, procurement) from time at an ESCO, an energy consultancy, an engineering firm or an energy-tech company. Have built things: scripts, models, prototypes or AI-assisted workflows, and can show us one. Prototype-quality code is enough; moving fast matters most. Are fluent with data tools (Excel, SQL or Python) and LLM tools, and can turn messy meter and bill data into something a customer acts on. Have run client work from scoping to outcome, and are as credible with a facilities manager as with a CFO. Can tell a compelling story with data, from raw numbers to insight to a recommendation someone signs off. You've originated work or supported deals, and want to get better at selling. Are energised to build a new product and service, to be on the front lines of building a new business, and to leave a legacy as part of a fast-moving team. Nice to have Experience with clean power deals (PPAs, VPPAs, fixed-price power contracts, and energy attribute certificates like RECs, GOs and REGOs). Hands-on work with utility bill, half-hourly or building management system data. A few years in consulting or advisory. Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles) Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so. What’s the interview process like? It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. jobs.title: Research Engineer, Agentic Systems
jobs.jd: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT RAMP LABS Ramp Labs is Ramp's AI research and engineering group. We post-train models on finance work, build the environments and evals they learn from, and ship them into the products 85,000+ companies use to move money. ABOUT THE ROLE Most agent work today is one agent, one trace, and a person reads the result. We're building systems where that stops working: thousands of agents fanned out over a large search space, each returning partial results, with an orchestrator that turns all of it into something useful: hundreds of merged PRs, a dataset, the input to another system, or something nobody has built yet. You'll design and run those systems: how work gets split, how agents coordinate, how results get deduplicated, verified and ranked, and what it all costs. The problems are general (agent swarms, agentic map-reduce, long-running fan-out workflows) and you'll own them from prototype to production. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Decide how the work gets done: how to break a problem down, what each agent sees, how many agents to run, and which model handles which step - Squeeze accuracy out of the models: context design, self-verification, voting and consensus across agents, and knowing when more agents stop helping - Measure quality without reading every trace: sampling, automated verification, and precision and recall on the final output - Drive down cost and latency per useful result: model routing, caching, early stopping, and smaller or fine-tuned models where they hold up - Turn one-off experiments into reusable workflows on our existing orchestration stack - Evaluate new models, inference setups and training approaches, and bring in what works WHAT YOU NEED - Experience building applied AI systems and LLM applications that shipped - Hands-on experience with multi-agent or high-fan-out LLM workloads: parallel agents, map-reduce over models, large batch inference - Strong engineering in Python; you build concurrent, distributed systems that hold up in production - Judgment about output: you decide what the end result should look like before you scale the swarm, and you can separate signal from agent noise - The habit of measuring: cost, yield, false-positive rate, and whether a change actually helped - Ownership: you can run a roadmap and a production system with little oversight - Clear written communication NICE-TO-HAVE - Built agent orchestration or job systems (Ray, Temporal, Modal or custom) - Used LLMs to search large spaces: codebases, document sets, logs or other large corpora - Post-training or hosting open-source models for high-volume inference - Distributed systems background - Public work we can look at: an agent framework, an open-source project, a write-up or a paper BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL) - Flexible PTO - Centralized home-office equipment ordering - Health and wellness stipend - Budget for intra-office travel - Weekly coffee stipend UNITED STATES - 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents - jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer II (Remote, US)
jobs.jd: About Sayari : Sayari is the judgment infrastructure for trustworthy AI in economic security and commercial risk. The Sayari Commercial World Model resolves 11.7B+ primary-source records from 250+ jurisdictions forming the ground truth of global commerce. A Judgment Ontology, encoding over a decade of investigative tradecraft, and Superconductor, an agentic orchestration platform, deliver AI that reasons like an expert analyst, shows its work, and traces every finding to its source. Trusted by U.S. Customs and Border Protection, HM Revenue & Customs, and Fortune 500 enterprises, Sayari is used by thousands of professionals across 35+ countries to secure supply chains and dismantle illicit networks. Headquartered in Washington, D.C., with offices in London, Singapore, Tokyo, and Tel Aviv. Forward Deployed Engineer II The Role Sayari’s largest customers, the biggest government agencies and Fortune 100 companies, are moving from data products to an agentic platform that runs their investigation and risk workflows end to end. As a Forward Deployed Engineer II, you are dedicated to those accounts. You own the technical win (demo, proof of concept, trial), then the deployment, then what comes after. The same engineer scopes the problem and ships it. You are equal parts engineer, strategist, and operator. You embed in the customer’s environment, build on Sayari’s agentic platform against their data and their workflows, and solve high-stakes problems that have no textbook answers. You are the conduit between the front lines and core engineering: what you learn in the field becomes what the platform does next. What You’ll Do Win the technical evaluation: design and run demos, proofs of concept, and trials that prove the platform on the customer’s own data. Define success criteria with the customer and hit them. Deploy the agentic platform: build agents, tools, and integrations on Sayari’s agentic platform inside the customer’s environment, and take them from trial to production. Embed and build: ship production Python, SQL, and integrations into customer persistence layers and analytics stacks. Own the relationship: serve as the primary technical authority for the account. Brief executives, analysts, and mission owners on outcomes. Triage and feed engineering: decide what is bespoke, what is reusable, and what belongs in the platform. Document capability gaps and drive them into the roadmap. Raise the bar: set delivery standards and review work for other engineers on your accounts. What We’re Looking For Required 5+ years in a client-facing technical role (forward deployed engineering, sales engineering, or technical consulting). 7-8+ total years of experience working in software engineering and/or solutions consulting A record of owning strategic deployments end to end, from technical win to production. Production Python, including the data manipulation ecosystem (Pandas). Deep experience having worked with SQL. Hands-on experience integrating and reasoning about REST APIs. Building and deploying on cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure) with containers (Docker, Kubernetes). You are a technology polyglot, you have worked across multiple tech stacks and enjoy getting the opportunity to navigate different coding languages, frameworks, and systems. AI-assisted coding tools (Cursor, Claude, or similar) as a daily part of how you work. Executive communication. You articulate technical concepts with clarity and conviction to engineers, analysts, and senior leaders alike. Problem solving in ambiguity, and the drive to parachute into new environments and learn new technologies on the fly. Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a technical field. Desired Hands-on experience building agentic or LLM systems: orchestration, tool use, retrieval, evaluation. Sovereign, air-gapped, or government cloud deployments. Modern data stack (Snowflake, Databricks) and workflow orchestrators (Airflow, Prefect). Graph data technologies and their query languages. Exposure to ML, NLP, or entity resolution. Experience in high-stakes domains: AML and financial crime, supply chain risk, or national security. How You Work You operate with extreme ownership. You build the bridge rather than flag the gap. You prefer a working prototype to a slide about one. You can scrap a month of work when the mission changes without losing momentum, and you hold yourself accountable for the outcome, not the activity. Logistics Travel and in-office time: 25 to 30% combined. Limitless growth and learning opportunities. Sayari is an equal opportunity employer and strongly encourages diverse candidates to apply. We believe diversity and inclusion mean our team members should reflect the diversity of the United States. Currently, Atreides focuses on providing high-fidelity data solutions to enable customers to derive insights quickly. We are a fast-moving, high-performance startup. Team Overview: We are a mission-driven team of technologists, data scientists, and analysts with backgrounds in operational intelligence, law enforcement, large multinationals, and cybersecurity operations. We obsess about designing products that will change the way global companies, governments and nonprofits protect themselves from external threats and global adversaries. Team Principles: At Atreides , we believe that teams work best when they: Remain curious and mission-driven in all aspects of our work Promote clear, direct, and transparent communication Embrace the 'measure twice, cut once' philosophy Value and encourage diverse ideas and technologies Lead with empathy in all interactions Position Overview: As a Senior Data Scientist at Atreides , you will lead deep analytical investigations that uncover structure, relationships, and operational insight from complex and high-volume data streams. Document software architecture, technical designs, and engineering decisions. Use AI tools as part of your daily workflow to accelerate analysis and development, while maintaining code quality and security. Strong background in statistical inference, anomaly detection, clustering, interaction modeling, or other analytical methods suited to large and heterogeneous datasets. Excellent communication, mentorship, and cross-functional collaboration skills, including the ability to explain AI-assisted results and their limitations to non-technical audiences. jobs.title: AI Engineering, Growth
jobs.jd:
Growth at HRtechX

The world’s most demanding investors are busy managing trillions, and ignore anything average. Are you excited by the challenge of making them act?

Are you looking to work in an exceptional entrepreneurial team with ambitious, motivated and extremely driven people? And do you want real ownership from your first week? If so, now is the time to apply for the Growth role at Private Equity Insights.

The mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors.

You will work in sprints and get fast execution under your skin. AI has completely changed the game: You will learn to deploy it to outperform a marketing team of 20+ people, while also learning the fundamentals of copywriting that makes elite investors act, get it to the right investor at a meaningful frequency and deploy what works across every marketing channel.

If you want an ambitious mission, real ownership and the fastest learning curve of your career: apply.

Why HRtechX

HRtechX is a world leading HRtech community, connecting industry executives, entrepreneurs and professionals. We are a start-up on a growth journey who help leaders evolve and create stronger businesses through people and technology. We aim to address the challenges and opportunities for HR and HR Tech. We bring together the most influential executives, investors, and entrepreneurs to share their insights on how technology will shape the future of HR, as well as forge long lasting partnerships and client relationships.

HRtechX is part of United Media (https://www.united-media.com/) which focuses on building large scale industry media and conferences products in sectors such as insurance, HR, private equity, retail, etc.

What we offer you

  • Master the highest bar in the world. Our audience is the world's most demanding investors. They ignore anything average. If your work can make them act, you can make anyone act.
  • Unlimited growth potential. You will get responsibility before you feel ready. That is how you grow fast. We strongly believe in and have a track record of promoting internally. You can expect coaching and development from leaders, peers and experts.
  • Skills that compound for life. Fast execution, copywriting, pricing, conversion optimisation, structured problem solving, and the ability to create impact anywhere in the business at scale.
  • Ownership from the very start. You own outcomes, not tasks. We agree the goal, and you find the way.
  • Travel opportunity. You will be joining our 10+ conferences.

What you will do

Responsibilities in this job will vary, however, feed into the mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors. They will be mostly centered around the following:

  • Build the audience. Identify, target, and convert every fund into our community, and make sure each one receives the right message, at the right time, and never one too many.
  • Own marketing channels that drive revenue. Through existing and new marketing channels, you execute activities that ultimately will drive revenue
  • Write copy that persuades. Every email, landing page and post. Become the best copywriter and leverage it at scale with AI.
  • Sprint, test, implement. Measure the impact of all experiments you run, test offers, copy, prices and pages until the numbers move.
  • Build systems, not one-offs. Anything you do twice becomes a playbook or an AI workflow, so the next win takes less effort than the last.
  • Do whatever it takes to win. Some days that means designing an AI workflow. Some days it means checking investors in at the registration desk at 7am. Nobody here is too good for the work that deliver value for investors and fund managers.

What we expect from you

  • 1 to 3 years of experience
  • Min. a bachelor or master degree with great results
  • A UK work permit. We do not sponsor visas.
  • Strong work ethic with a sense of urgency
  • Exceptional drive and desire to be the best at what you do
  • Proactive approach and sense of ownership/responsibility of everything you do
  • A humble approach and share our passion for building companies and developing people
  • Interested in continuous learning and proactively searching for ways to optimise

Practical details

Full-time, in person from our London office (WeWork), 5 days a week. Expect to travel for work about 20 days a year. The start date is flexible.

jobs.jd: The Amazon Center for Quantum Computing (CQC) is seeking an Applied Scientist to research and design superconducting qubit devices and circuit elements for scalable quantum processors. You will evaluate alternative processor architectures and packaging approaches against quantitative scaling metrics, and work closely with the co-located processor design team so that what we learn about future systems improves the systems being built today. jobs.title: Senior Full Stack Engineer - Agentic Engineering
jobs.jd: Job Description The Opportunity Adobe is reimagining the future of creativity — where generative AI, intelligent agents, and human imagination work hand in hand. As a Senior Full Stack Engineer, Agentic Product, you will be a key technical contributor for Adobe's up-and-coming AI-native experience that brings generative models, creative intelligence, and decades of differentiated Adobe capabilities together for hundreds of millions of creators. You will own hands-on buildout of the agent across the full stack and across Adobe's target platforms, from desktop and mobile to web and embedded surfaces. You will help reshape the way the team works in the age of agentic engineering. And you will be getting in on the ground floor to help shape the team and its practices. This is a rare opportunity to build the engineering foundations of Adobe's soon-to-be most visible AI product — from model integration and agentic reasoning patterns, to production infrastructure and cross-platform delivery. The right person brings deep, hands-on full-stack expertise, proven experience shipping agentic systems, a genuine enthusiasm for transforming how engineering itself is done with AI tools like Claude Code and Codex, and the craft to write production-quality code that holds up over time. What you'll do Own full-stack implementation across Adobe's Agentic Product — from LLM integration and agentic reasoning layers, to API surfaces, client runtimes, and platform-specific delivery on desktop, mobile, and web. Contribute to the production buildout of the agent: translating prototype-quality capabilities into robust, scalable, maintainable systems that meet Adobe's quality and reliability bar for a large, diverse audience. Drive hands-on implementation of high-leverage components — including model orchestration, tool use, multi-step task execution, context and memory management, and agent evaluation infrastructure. Champion the adoption of AI-assisted engineering practices — using tools like Claude Code, Codex, and emerging agentic development platforms to accelerate implementation, raise code quality, and fundamentally change how the team ships. Model new workflows where AI is a first-class collaborator in the development process. Contribute to developer experience: tooling, local development loops, CI/CD ergonomics, and the scaffolding that lets a team move fast and confidently in a fast-moving AI product environment. jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist - Demand Forecast (f/m/d)
jobs.location: Lille, Upline, Nord; Paris, Paris France
jobs.jd:
About Decathlon

Decathlon aims to become the best sports digital platform and open ecosystem in the world. We want to enable customers to experience Decathlon through many local sport-centric experiences by connecting many third-party actors and services, in a secure and performant way.

Our digital teams bring together more than 5000 collaborators are united to build and scale digital products with the aim to always deliver the best value to our users. With a presence in more than 70 countries, Decathlon is committed to innovation, sustainability, and customer satisfaction.

Job Description

Decathlon is seeking a talented and experienced Data Scientist to join our Demand and Assortment Planning team within the Supply Chain department. As a Senior Data Scientist, you will play a critical role in developing AI models into production and providing insights/recommendations to optimise demand forecasting and assortment planning processes. We welcome candidates with expertise in time series forecasting and a passion for leveraging data to drive business decisions.

Responsibilities

  • Analyse and study historical sales data and market trends to forecast demand for Decathlon products.
  • Develop and implement advanced statistical models and machine learning algorithms for demand forecasting and assortment planning, including foundation models. 
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Supply Chain Business, Engineering, and Product Development to align Data and AI efforts with business objectives.
  • Evaluate and improve existing forecasting models and methodologies to enhance accuracy and efficiency.
  • Communicate insights and recommendations to stakeholders through clear and concise data visualisations and presentations.
  • Stay updated on industry trends and emerging technologies in data science and supply chain management.

Hard Skills

  • Proficiency in statistical analysis, forecasting, machine learning techniques, time series, time series foundation models and time series analysis (stationarity, decomposition, drift, anomaly detection).
  • Experience with programming languages such as Python, Spark, TensorFlow, Pytorch for data analysis and modelling.
  • Strong knowledge of data manipulation and visualisation tools such as pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, or ggplot2.
  • Familiarity with database systems and querying languages (e.g., SQL, PySpark) for data extraction and manipulation.
  • Experience with demand forecasting and inventory optimisation software/tools is a plus.
  • Experience with Generative AI is a plus.

Soft Skills

  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities with a keen attention to detail.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills to work effectively in cross-functional teams.
  • Ability to translate complex technical concepts into actionable insights for non-technical stakeholders.
  • Self-motivated with a proactive approach to learning and professional development.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced and dynamic environment with changing priorities.
  • Initiative and proactivity

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, or related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in data science, statistical modelling, or related fields.
  • Proficiency in Python for data analysis and modelling.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's or Ph.D. degree in Data Science, Statistics, Operations Research, or related field.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in Data Science.
  • Experience in demand forecasting, inventory optimisation, or supply chain analytics.
  • Familiarity with Agile methodologies and project management tools.
  • Previous experience in the retail or e-commerce industry is a plus.
  • Experience in implementing Generative AI to enhance forecasting, alongside optimising business or organisational processes for product delivery.

Technical Environment

  • Execution Engine: Databricks, AWS EKS, Sagemaker
  • Payload: Python, Spark, Scikit-Learn, Tensorflow / Pytorch, Pyspark 
  • CICD: Github Actions
  • Serving: Docker, Protobuf, gRPC
  • Model registry, Model Tracking: MLFlow
  • Orchestration:  Airflow
  • Documentation / code: Git, Confluence
  • Data Visualisation: Tableau
  • Agentic & Gen Ai : Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform

DECATHLON DIGITAL 

Imaginez si la technologie nous permettait de repousser les frontières et d'offrir des expériences sportives inédites. C'est précisément notre ambition chez Decathlon Digital ! Nous sommes une équipe de plus de 5 000 experts en ingénierie logicielle, gestion de produits, données, cloud et cybersécurité, répartis à Paris, Lille et Amsterdam. Ensemble, nous créons la plus vaste plateforme sportive numérique, en exploitant les innovations technologiques pour optimiser la chaîne de valeur, concevoir des expériences connectées et donner une seconde vie à nos produits.

Changeons la donne pour de bon. Notre passion du sport nous guide et nous voulons qu’elle perdure. C’est pourquoi nous nous engageons à bâtir un modèle technologique plus durable, en réduisant notre impact direct sur l'environnement, et en créant un espace sûr et inclusif pour apprendre et nous épanouir ensemble. Rejoins l’équipe et façonnons le futur du sport.

jobs.title: Senior Applied AI Scientist, Commerce Foundation Models
jobs.jd: Who We Are You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today. We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover. Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI. Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate. Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale. About the team Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people. About the role We’re looking for experienced applied scientists in two tracks: pre-training, and post-training and continual learning. Each scientist will own a focused research direction within a track. The areas below describe the team’s research agenda; we are looking for depth in one or more of them. The role involves designing experiments, writing the code to run them, analysing results and developing training methods that other teams can use. Scientists own the research questions, training objectives and evidence needed to decide whether a change works, and work with ML engineers to turn successful experiments into reliable training runs. We are a team of around 30 engineers with a flat structure, working directly with portfolio companies to define problems, evaluate models and bring successful work into production. In the first three months, the expectation is to establish strong baselines in a chosen research area, develop and evaluate an improvement, and work with the relevant teams to test it in a downstream application. Track 1: Pre-training This track focuses on continued pre-training of open-weight models on commerce data, including how we represent that data, allocate training compute and transfer capabilities to smaller models. Research areas include: Studying scaling behaviour, data mixtures and compute allocation to decide what goes into the next training run. Developing mid-training methods, including data refinement, annealing schedules, context extension and alignment between text and semantic IDs for users, items and merchants. Designing training sequences from user histories, merchant catalogues and market data, and studying how representations transfer across companies, languages and commerce categories. Building synthetic data pipelines and measuring their contribution through controlled comparisons with real data. Distilling the base model into smaller models, including through on-policy distillation, and measuring the trade-offs between quality, inference cost and latency. Developing evaluations that help select pre-training runs and predict downstream performance, including checks for temporal leakage, generalisation to new users and items, and retention of existing capabilities. Tabular foundation models are a possible specialisation: pre-training and in-context learning on structured commerce data, using synthetic and real tables and comparing results with established tabular methods. Relevant experience includes continued pre-training or mid-training, data mixture research, scaling laws, tokenisation, entity representations, distillation, or tabular foundation models such as TabPFN and TabICL. Track 2: Post-training and continual learning This track focuses on adapting LCM to commerce tasks and learning from interactions after deployment. The goal is to turn signals from a continuous stream of billions of user sessions across the portfolio into regular updates to model weights, while retaining the capabilities the model has already learned. Research areas include: Developing post-training methods using supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation such as DPO, and reinforcement learning with verifiable or learned rewards, including GRPO and PPO. Learning from session histories, searches, clicks, purchases, repeat orders and operator feedback. This includes data selection, credit assignment and reward design that account for exposure bias, delayed outcomes and the difference between observed engagement and incremental business value. Studying how to combine new interactions with historical data, how frequently to update models, when an update is ready for deployment, and how to preserve performance as user behaviour and catalogues change. Building RL environments with simulated users, catalogues and multi-step commerce tasks, including inspecting trajectories, validating rewards and testing whether improvements in simulation transfer to real interactions. jobs.jd:

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer in GitLab's Agent Foundations stage, you'll go beyond using AI tools. You'll help build the foundations for GitLab's agentic AI experiences: the platform that lets AI agents work across the whole software delivery lifecycle, not just write code. That covers how agents are created, shared and connected to tools inside and outside GitLab, how they run, and how their work shows up and can be observed across GitLab.

In this role you'll work closely with engineers across the stage and other AI Engineering teams. This is a high-visibility area where GitLab's core platform meets its AI strategy.

What you'll do

  • Develop, ship and maintain features for the Duo Agent Platform in the GitLab monolith (Ruby) and, where needed, the AI Gateway (Python). Keep them secure, well-tested and performant.
  • Work with Product Management, UX, frontend, backend and AI specialists to refine requirements and ship improvements in small iterations.
  • Design, implement and review GraphQL and REST APIs and the backend logic behind them, with reliable, scalable and clear contracts for clients.
  • Improve and extend automated testing (RSpec and other frameworks) to strengthen quality and give developers faster feedback.
  • Share standards, patterns and learnings with other engineers to raise the bar for responsible AI integration and evidence-driven engineering.
  • Join Tier 2 on-call rotations to troubleshoot production issues, contribute to root cause analysis, and improve observability and resiliency.
  • Keep an eye on the competitive landscape to help keep GitLab's agent platform best-in-class.

What you'll bring

  • Experience building and maintaining production Ruby on Rails applications, including background jobs, APIs and data models.
  • Comfort working across the stack in a mature codebase. Familiarity with Python backends and/or Vue frontends is a plus.
  • Skill in designing or extending REST and/or GraphQL APIs with attention to scalability, maintainability and backward compatibility.
  • Real enthusiasm for AI and hands-on experience using AI tools in your daily work. Experience designing and shipping AI-powered backend features or integrations is a plus.
  • Proven SQL and experience with relational databases such as PostgreSQL, including writing efficient queries and data modeling.
  • Experience finding and fixing performance bottlenecks in applications.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including technical proposals and documentation, in a remote, async, cross-functional team.

About the team

The Agent Foundations stage builds the foundations for GitLab's agentic AI experiences. We provide the platform, catalog and execution features that help teams deliver resilient agents and flows to customers. The stage has three groups: Agent Developer, AI Catalog and Agent Execution, they provide the core harness for GitLab’s agents, the tools Agent’s need to interact with GitLab as well as ways to configure and execute Agents across GitLab.

Our engineers work async-first across EMEA and AMER timezones. We work with teams across AI engineering and the rest of GitLab so the Duo Agent Platform can power many of GitLab's AI features.

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist - Healthcare AI & Data Harmonization - Remote (Philadelphi
jobs.jd: Req ID: 398007 NTT DATA strives to hire exceptional, innovative and passionate individuals who want to grow with us. If you want to be part of an inclusive, adaptable, and forward-thinking organization, apply now. We are currently seeking a Senior Data Scientist - Healthcare AI & Data Harmonization - Remote to join our team in Philadelphia, Plano, Pennsylvania (US-PA), United States (US). Senior Data Scientist – Healthcare AI & Data Harmonization Position Overview We are seeking an experienced Senior Data Scientist to lead the architecture, development, and scaling of an enterprise data harmonization platform focused on transforming large volumes of complex healthcare and medical data into standardized, structured, and actionable information. This individual will serve as a senior technical subject matter expert, designing and implementing intelligent AI-driven pipelines to ingest, interpret, normalize, and map heterogeneous structured and unstructured datasets, including clinical, genomic, pathology, and operational data. The role will leverage advanced Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), Natural Language Processing (NLP), semantic search, and biomedical ontologies to automate complex data mapping and schema alignment at enterprise scale. The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in machine learning architecture, transformer models, distributed computing, and AI infrastructure, including optimization and deployment across specialized hardware accelerators such as NVIDIA GPUs and Google TPUs. They will work closely with Data Engineering, Bioinformatics, and Regulatory/Compliance teams to deliver scalable, production-ready AI and MLOps solutions. Key Responsibilities AI Architecture & Data Harmonization Define the technical architecture and roadmap for an enterprise-scale data harmonization and intelligent mapping platform. Design and develop AI-powered pipelines to ingest, process, normalize, and map heterogeneous clinical, genomic, biomedical, and operational datasets. Automate complex schema alignment, semantic matching, and data transformation across structured and unstructured data sources. Establish scalable approaches for processing multi-terabyte datasets while maintaining data quality, accuracy, and performance. LLM, NLP & AI Model Development Architect, fine-tune, and deploy domain-specific Large Language Models, transformer architectures, and embedding models for healthcare data interpretation and semantic alignment. Develop advanced NLP capabilities, including Named Entity Recognition (NER), entity linking, relation extraction, and clinical information extraction. Implement semantic search and retrieval-based approaches to improve medical terminology recognition, contextual understanding, and automated data mapping. Evaluate and optimize model performance, accuracy, inference latency, and computational efficiency. GPU/TPU Acceleration & Distributed AI Computing Lead the optimization and deployment of complex AI/ML workloads using specialized hardware accelerators, including NVIDIA GPUs and Google TPUs. Leverage acceleration and distributed computing technologies to support high-throughput model training, fine-tuning, and inference. Optimize transformer and NLP workloads using technologies such as CUDA, TensorRT, Triton Inference Server, DeepSpeed, and vLLM. Establish scalable infrastructure and deployment patterns to support enterprise-level AI processing requirements. Medical Ontology & Semantic Data Mapping Lead the development of automated mapping solutions that align diverse healthcare data sources with established biomedical vocabularies and ontologies. Establish standardized approaches for schema mapping, terminology normalization, semantic validation, and data quality assurance. Work with healthcare data standards and models, including OMOP CDM, FHIR, UMLS, SNOMED CT, RxNorm, and LOINC. Develop validation frameworks and quality controls to ensure consistency, traceability, and accuracy across mapped datasets. MLOps, Platform Engineering & Technical Leadership Partner with Data Engineers, Bioinformaticians, and Regulatory/Compliance teams to deliver production-ready AI and data processing solutions. Design and implement scalable MLOps pipelines supporting model deployment, monitoring, versioning, evaluation, and continuous retraining. jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist
jobs.jd: About Orakl Oncology At Orakl Oncology, we are accelerating the development of oncology treatments. Today, fewer than 5% of new cancer drugs succeed in clinical trials. Clearly, new methods are needed. We combine cutting-edge biology and AI to build the next generation of insight platforms with the world's largest cohort of patient tumor avatars. These avatars fuel our AI-powered predictive engine, helping to anticipate clinical trial outcomes, validate therapies, and uncover new drug candidates. Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalised. We collaborate with top hospitals, research institutes, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by leading investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology. About the Role Improving the quantity and quality of biological data is one of the most challenging bottlenecks to accelerate the rate of scientific discoveries in biology. In our labs at Orakl Oncology, we grow cancer cells from real patients, at scale, to generate our own experimental data. This data is deeply multi-modal and ranges from microscopic images, experimental metadata, to viability data and beyond. We are looking for a Senior Data Scientist to own the wet-lab data chain end-to-end: from raw instrument and screening outputs through to processing pipelines. You will work on the canonical data model for lab data, as well as building the validated, analysis-ready datasets and tools our scientists and downstream teams rely on. This is a high-ownership, hands-on role at the intersection of data science, production engineering, and experimental biology. You will ship and maintain code in production, define how we model experimental data, and build the quality controls and feedback loops that let the lab catch errors early and iterate faster. This is a role where you are expected to be in the lab, talk to scientists and lab technicians on a day-to-day basis. You will see how science is done in the lab, and then think hard about how to improve its impact. If you’re excited by complex workflows and the friction of real-life lab work, as well the power of data and AI, this position is for you. What You'll Do Own the lab-based data generation pipelines: to enable data transfer at scale from the lab to the cloud. This will involve building and improving production codebases that turn high-throughput experimental readouts into validated insights. Facilitate lab operations : Maintain and/or build tools to accelerate the work of Orakl Oncology scientists. Define and own the canonical data model: Design the unified data model that structures our data and is adopted across teams, ensuring data can be joined across modalities: experimental, clinical, omics, and clinical-trial event reporting. Design and own data quality pipeline: Build QC that flags data quality at transfer time, and turn it into feedback loops so scientists can spot experimental errors early and integrate checks into their routine. Support lab initiatives: such as automation initiatives, the development of experimental tooling to help lab scientists and technicians. Drive operational efficiency: make sure that wet lab work is optimized to benefit the most from our resources (human and experimental) and ensure efficient contract and research delivery. Minimum Qualifications Masters or PhD degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Bioengineering, or a related quantitative field. 3+ years of experience as a data scientist, with a proven track record of shipping and maintaining Python code in production Strong hacker and tinkerer mindset. You like building things that have a real world effects. Excellent proficiency in Python and SQL , and solid data-engineering skills: pipeline design and orchestration (Airflow, Dagster, dbt, or equivalent), version control (Git), testing/CI, and observability. Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and data-storage best practices. Comfortable working with noisy, real-world experimental data and directly alongside non-technical scientists. Preferred Qualifications Hands-on experience with experimental, assay, or high-throughput screening data. Working knowledge of biology, ideally in oncology, cell biology, or drug discovery. Experience with image analysis / computer vision applied to microscopy data. Familiarity with lab data systems / LIMS (e.g. Benchling) and experimental workflows. Who You Are Curious and autonomous: you dig into scientists' bottlenecks, connect the dots across teams, and ship without waiting for perfect specifications. A fast shipper: you get working solutions into production and iterate, rather than polishing in isolation. A strong communicator: you gather needs from and explain your work to non-technical scientists, acting as the data bridge across the lab and beyond. At ease in a complex and interdisciplinary environment: you thrive with messy data, evolving priorities, and external constraints that come with a science-first, non-pure-tech setting. Why Join Orakl Own the wet-lab data backbone of a techbio platform from the ground up: your work directly shapes how we discover and validate cancer therapies. Sit at one of the most interdisciplinary intersections in techbio: data science, production engineering, and experimental oncology, side-by-side every day. jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, LLM Inference Optimization
jobs.jd:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer on the Applied AI team at Nebius Token Factory, you will own model and endpoint optimization from model artifacts through production deployment. Your work will span model internals, quantization and model compression, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, inference engines, serving architecture, and benchmarking to improve latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, and cost per token while preserving quality and reliability.

You will work with kernel and platform engineers to investigate serving problems, compare configurations, and resolve performance and quality regressions. You will evaluate model- and engine-level optimizations together with distributed inference designs, including request routing, scheduling, prefill/decode coordination, and multi-node GPU execution. Your improvements will be validated through reproducible benchmarks and safe production rollouts under real-world workloads.

Your responsibilities

  • Own optimization projects for specific model families, customer endpoints, or serving backends.
  • Compare inference engines and recommend serving configurations suited to individual workloads.
  • Diagnose model-quality and performance regressions during production rollouts.
  • Improve LLM and VLM endpoint latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, quality, and cost per token.
  • Deploy, configure, benchmark, and extend engines such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo.
  • Develop production model-compression workflows covering quantization, quantization-aware training, distillation, low-bit serving, and accuracy recovery.
  • Implement or integrate speculative decoding, draft-model approaches, KV-cache optimization, prefix caching, chunked prefill, continuous batching, and disaggregated prefill/decode serving. For prefill–decode disaggregation (PDD), evaluate KV-cache transfer, worker placement, and capacity balancing to determine which workloads benefit from the architecture.
  • Design and improve LLM request routers and scheduling policies that balance worker utilization, queueing, request characteristics, and KV-cache locality while meeting latency and reliability targets.
  • Scale dense and mixture-of-experts inference across multiple GPU nodes. Select and tune tensor, pipeline, data, and expert parallelism—including wide expert parallelism (WideEP)—with attention to hardware topology, expert load balance, and communication overhead.
  • Build reproducible benchmark harnesses measuring TTFT, TPOT, tokens per second per GPU, p95/p99 latency, GPU memory, reliability, and cost per token. Validate architecture choices under representative traffic and consistent GPU budgets.
  • Collaborate with GPU kernel and platform engineers to trace bottlenecks across model code, kernels, runtime, scheduler, gateway, and cluster layers.
  • Produce design documents, performance reports, rollout plans, and customer-facing technical explanations.

Must-haves

  • Strong engineering skills in Python and PyTorch.
  • Hands-on experience deploying or optimizing LLM, VLM, or high-throughput transformer inference.
  • Practical knowledge of at least one modern inference stack, such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, NVIDIA Dynamo, Ray Serve, KServe, or an equivalent internal system.
  • A strong understanding of transformer inference bottlenecks involving KV cache, attention, memory bandwidth, batching, parallelism, and long-context serving.
  • Ability to quantify trade-offs among latency, throughput, quality, utilization, and cost.
  • Experience designing or optimizing distributed inference system architecture, with hands-on work in one or more areas such as request routing, distributed scheduling, PDD, multi-node inference, or expert parallelism.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills across research, kernel, infrastructure, product, and customer teams.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience with quantization-aware training, post-training quantization, FP8, INT8, INT4, NVFP4, MXFP4, AWQ, GPTQ, or SmoothQuant.
  • Experience with distillation, speculative decoding, EAGLE, Medusa, multi-token prediction, or related inference acceleration methods.
  • Experience supporting agentic workloads involving tool calling, structured outputs, streaming APIs, high concurrency, and multi-step orchestration.
  • Familiarity with CUDA or Triton; the role does not require kernel engineering to be the candidate’s primary specialization.
  • Contributions to open-source projects such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, FlashInfer, LMCache, PyTorch, Triton, Ray, or KServe.

jobs.title: Senior ML Applied Scientist , Frontier AI Startup Team
jobs.jd: AI-native startups now train their own models, post-train open-weight models for their products, and serve inference at volumes where cost per output decides their margins. The startup team of the AWS Frontier AI Services puts applied scientists to work directly with those founders and their engineers. We're hiring a Senior Applied Scientist in North America to own those engagements with our strategists end to end: scope the problem with the founding team, design and run the experiments, and ship working code into the startup's stack on AWS. The problems are open-ended and the timelines run in weeks, so your scientific judgment sets both the approach and the bar for done. Key job responsibilities - Work directly with founders, CTOs and ML leads at AI startups to define the problem and agree on a production target and an evaluation plan. Then deliver against them in six-to-twelve-week engagements, with the startup's own engineers working alongside you. - Improve model quality for the startup's use case by post-training open-weight models. That covers supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, reinforcement learning (for example GRPO), distillation, and the synthetic data and evaluation sets that show whether it worked. - Cut training and inference cost and latency on NVIDIA GPUs and AWS Trainium. Profile where the compute goes, apply quantization, speculative decoding, KV-cache reuse, batching, parallelism and kernel-level tuning, and measure cost per output before and after. - Invent new methods when published ones fall short of the customer's target, and publish the results at peer-reviewed venues, on AWS blogs and as open-source code. - Turn each engagement into assets the next one can reuse: reference implementations, evaluation harnesses and playbooks. Take the gaps you find in Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker and AWS Trainium back to those service teams as specific requests. - Raise the science bar on the team. Review experiment designs and code, mentor scientists and engineers, and help account teams and strategists judge which startup requests need a scientist. A day in the life You start the day on a call with the CTO of a robotics startup whose vision-language model misses objects in low light. Before anyone changes the model, you agree on an evaluation set built from their own camera footage. Mid-morning you check an overnight reinforcement-learning run for another startup: reward is up but two task categories regressed, so you write up why and what to try next. After lunch you join an AWS account manager and a GenAI strategist to scope a request from a voice AI company that needs lower inference latency before it scales up. You leave with a two-week profiling plan and one go/no-go metric. You end the day reviewing a teammate's experiment design and editing a workshop paper drawn from last quarter's engagement. About the team We're applied scientists and GenAI strategists working as one team with venture-backed, AI-native startups, from the first discovery call to a model running in production. The work spans large language and vision-language models, agents, voice, multimodal retrieval and physical AI, including world and action models. We judge an engagement by what the startup ships. Startups make platform decisions in weeks, so we scope quickly, share results early, and say plainly when something isn't working. This role focuses on startups in North America. You'll work with AWS account teams, solutions architects and service teams, and with Amazon's wider science community. - PhD, or Master's degree and 6+ years of applied research experience - Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language - Experience with modeling tools such as R, scikit-learn, Spark MLLib, MxNet, Tensorflow, numpy, scipy etc. - Experience with large scale distributed systems such as Hadoop, Spark etc. - 6+ years of building machine learning models for business application experience Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Research Engineer, Foundation Model (Multimodal Fusion & Distillation)
jobs.jd: Our Mission At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient. We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today! The Role You will build the parts of LEA, our foundation model of the physical world, where field data is the input. LEA takes in cameras, infrared, thermal, lidar and robot state natively, around the clock, on real security sites. We stand on the best open models for the encoders and the reasoning head and do not pretrain from scratch. Your work goes where nobody else can do it: fusing every sensor into one stream, teaching an open vision-language model to reason over that stream, and distilling a fast model that sees every frame. This is the first engineer dedicated to the model track, so you will also set how we train, evaluate and ship models. You will work with our Command Centre and Robot Autonomy teams to get what you train running on site appliances and robots, and you will see it tested at 03:00 in the rain. What You'll Work On Native encoders: adapt the best open vision and point-cloud foundation models to RGB, IR, thermal and lidar, one encoder per sensor, raw stream in. Fusion: build the layer that aligns every sensor in time and space into one token stream, trained on time-aligned multi-sensor field data that exists nowhere else. Slow head: fine-tune an open frontier vision-language model to reason over fused sensor tokens instead of pictures. Fast head: distil a small model from the slow head's calls on our own events, so every frame is seen and only hard cases escalate. Evaluation: held-out sites, night and thermal slices, regression gates. A model that is worse anywhere does not ship. Training machinery: multi-GPU training, data loaders for multi-sensor clips, experiment tracking and reproducible runs. Who We're Looking For A research engineer who has shipped multimodal models, not only published them. You know when an open model is good enough and when to build, you measure on the slice that matters before claiming a number, and you care whether the model works on a real site, not only on a benchmark. Your Background 4+ years training and fine-tuning large vision or multimodal models, or a PhD plus industry experience. Strong PyTorch, comfortable with multi-GPU and multi-node training. Hands-on fine-tuning of vision-language models (instruction tuning, parameter-efficient methods, full fine-tunes). Experience with knowledge distillation or model compression for deployment. Work with video or non-RGB sensors: thermal, infrared, lidar or radar. Evaluation discipline and solid software engineering hygiene. Nice to Have Point-cloud or 3D foundation models. Self-supervised and latent-prediction methods (JEPA-style). Edge deployment with TensorRT or similar. Robotics or field data collection. Publications at top ML, vision or robotics venues. What We Offer Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end. Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence. jobs.jd:

In this role, you will collaborate closely with the production, hardware engineering, and firmware/software teams, as well as operations, ensuring that every platform transitions smoothly from an airframe concept into a fully validated flying robot ready for deployment. Responsibilities and Duties

  • Operate in a highly hands-on environment with evolving system requirements, rapidly iterating across hardware and software integration challenges.
  • Manage software releases and perform firmware flashing and configuration using PX4 or adjacent autopilot ecosystems, including sensor calibration, ESC tuning, and system bring-up.
  • Provide deep avionics and airframe expertise, including autopilot tuning, sensor and payload integration, power systems and airworthiness considerations.
  • Work independently to troubleshoot integration and flight-readiness issues while collaborating cross-functionally with hardware engineering, firmware/software teams, operations, and QC engineering to escalate complex challenges when required.
  • Act as the primary technical authority in customer engagements, translating mission requirements into concrete system architectures and demonstrable solutions built on AuterionOS and Skynode.
  • Participate in flight testing activities to validate platform stability, safety, and mission performance, resolving technical issues often directly in the field during customer trials and demonstrations.
  • Contribute to technical documentation and continuous improvement of engineering processes.
  • Feed customer and market requirements back into product and engineering teams to influence the roadmap of the Auterion stack.

Qualifications and Skills

  • Degree in Software, Electrical, Mechanical, Aerospace or Robotics Engineering, or a related field
  • Working proficiency in C/C++ and Python: you can read, debug and patch existing code and write small tools and scripts
  • Comfortable in Linux environments, including the command line, logs, Docker and basic networking (IP, TCP/UDP)
  • Hands-on hardware-software integration: system bring-up, wiring and connectors, and embedded interfaces (UART, CAN, I2C, SPI) at a practical level
  • Structured troubleshooting: you can isolate whether a problem is software, hardware, configuration or RF, often under time pressure in the field
  • Strong communicator: you can explain technical issues clearly to customers and operators, and report findings back to engineering in a way they can act on
  • Willing to travel and work on-site with customers, including at test ranges and in field environments
  • EU citizenship (required for security clearance and customer requirements)

Nice-to-have

  • Experience with PX4 or ArduPilot, MAVLink, QGroundControl or mission planning tools
  • UAV flight testing and validation in operational environments
  • Experience with datalinks and radio systems
  • Previous customer-facing or field engineering role, especially with defense or government customers
  • German language skills

Benefits

  • Flexible working hours
  • Stock Options
  • Generous holiday allowance
  • Pension plan 
  • Extended social security package 
  • Enhanced maternity & paternity leave

jobs.title: Applied Scientist, Quantum Device Integration, Amazon's Center for Quantum Computing, Device Team
jobs.jd: The Amazon Web Services (AWS) Center for Quantum Computing (CQC) in Pasadena, CA, is hiring an Applied Scientist to lead integration research and development for superconducting quantum devices. You will design, model, and test the chip-to-chip, chip-to-package, and signal-delivery interfaces that let superconducting quantum computers scale, and you will characterize integrated assemblies at cryogenic temperatures to learn how integration choices affect qubit performance, yield, and manufacturability. You will join a multi-disciplinary team of theoretical and experimental physicists, materials scientists, and hardware and software engineers working at the forefront of quantum computing. You will carry integration technologies from concept through hardware demonstration, build the test standards and automation that make results reproducible across devices, and collaborate with fabrication, hardware, and circuit design engineers to remove the dominant sources of yield loss. You will also contribute to multi-year roadmap planning for integration and scaling capabilities and help establish the scientific foundation for this capability area within the Device team. Key job responsibilities In this role you will develop the integration technologies that let superconducting quantum computers scale. Your work will span four connected areas: - Integration research and development: Design, model, and test integration solutions for superconducting quantum devices, including chip-to-chip, chip-to-package, and signal-delivery interfaces. Build electromagnetic, thermal, and mechanical models to predict and optimize performance, and characterize integrated assemblies at cryogenic temperatures. - Scaling technologies: Develop and evaluate approaches to scaling superconducting quantum hardware against yield, reusability, manufacturability, and scalability, and carry the most promising ones from concept through hardware demonstration. - Test standards and automation: Define test standards that give rigorous, reproducible measurements of how integration affects qubit coherence, loss, and crosstalk. Automate data collection and reporting against these standards so characterization scales across devices and configurations. - Yield and manufacturability: Work with fabrication, hardware, printed circuit board, and circuit design engineers to identify and remove the largest sources of yield loss and integration uncertainty, and to design processes and components that are reused across device generations and manufactured at scale. About the team The Device team at the AWS Center for Quantum Computing designs, builds, and measures the superconducting quantum devices at the heart of our processors, and develops the integration and packaging that turn individual devices into working systems. You will work alongside physicists, materials scientists, and hardware and software engineers across design, fabrication, measurement, and theory, in a lab built for rapid iteration from concept to cryogenic test. Our mission is to bring these agents to life inside real customer environments — testing them against real data, real workflows, and real use cases. We're early in the agent lifecycle, which means the work here is hands-on, fast-moving, and genuinely entrepreneurial: you'll often help write the playbook for how Workday deploys a new agent, rather than follow one that already exists. If you want to be close to the product at the exact moment it's taking shape, and to see your fieldwork directly change the product, this is the team to build inside.
